+
+== Amendment (2026-06-04): three release-blockers gate marketplace publishing
+
+A team review of the three integrations (`flatbars-lsp`, the VS Code extension,
+the JetBrains plugin) confirmed the two-layer design of this ADR but found the
+*release readiness* is gated on process and seam gaps, not features. Until the
+three blockers below are closed, the extensions are **not** to be published to the
+VS Code Marketplace / Open VSX / JetBrains Marketplace. The decisions:
+
+. *Activation is unverified, so it is release-blocking (VS Code).* The extension
+  ships `pass:[activationEvents: []]` (`editors/vscode/package.json`). The TextMate
+  floor is declarative and paints regardless, but the language *client* — and thus
+  the entire LSP ceiling (semantic tokens + diagnostics) — starts in `activate()`,
+  which has no trigger; VS Code does not auto-infer `onLanguage` for a contributed
+  language. The smoke test cannot catch this: it spawns the server process
+  directly, bypassing activation. *Decision:* declare explicit
+  `pass:[onLanguage:{rawbars,minbars,fullbars,maxbars,flatbars}]` activation events,
+  and add a *real-IDE* test that asserts both a semantic token and a published
+  diagnostic actually surface in a running editor (not just that the server speaks
+  LSP over a pipe).
+
+. *The JVM/LSP path compiles on no CI machine, so it is release-blocking
+  (JetBrains).* `test:jetbrains` validates the bundled JS transport (descriptors,
+  grammar canonicality, an LSP round-trip) but never compiles Kotlin; the
+  Ultimate-only LSP layer (`-PwithLsp`, the platform LSP API absent from the open
+  SDK) is built nowhere we control. *Decision:* add a path-filtered CI job
+  (`editors/jetbrains/**`) running `gradle buildPlugin -PwithLsp` on JDK 17, plus a
+  real-IDE VS Code run, so neither client ships code that has only ever been
+  type-checked by hand.
+
+. *The "one vocabulary, three consumers" seams are ungated, so they are
+  release-blocking (shared).* The contract this ADR rests on has unchecked joints:
+  `lspEmitKinds` (`editors/token-vocabulary.json`) drives the sparse-correction
+  design but is pinned by no test — adding `expr` to it would silently flatten
+  `pass:[{{{x}}}]` to one colour, the exact failure Decision 1's floor design
+  guards against, with every gate green; `check:tmgrammar` asserts tag boundaries
+  and literals but *not* that the grammar's scope names still match the vocabulary's
+  `tmScopes`; and the embedded engine bundle (`lab/vendor/flatbars-engine.mjs`,
+  re-exported by `editors/lsp/src/engine.mjs`) carries no API-version the server can
+  assert. Packaging compounds it: the two `sync-assets.mjs` scripts call `esbuild`
+  *unpinned* and duplicate the dialect list by hand, undercutting the
+  byte-reproducibility `check:bundle` enforces (it pins `esbuild@0.23.0`).
+  *Decision (implemented):* add a vocabulary-integrity gate, `check:vocab`
+  (`scripts/check-vocab.mjs`, in `npm test`), asserting engine kinds ≡ vocabulary
+  kinds — witnessed by the `check:highlight` corpus, so there is no second corpus —
+  the *pinned* `lspEmitKinds` set, the LSP legend derivation, and grammar scope
+  names ⊇ vocabulary `tmScopes`; and pin + centralise the packaging `esbuild` in
+  `editors/shared/sync.mjs` (the shared bundle step + single-sourced language set,
+  pinned to the `esbuild@0.23.0` `gen:bundle` already uses). The "engine-shape
+  compatibility" the bundle API-version idea targeted is met by this gate (kinds ≡
+  vocabulary ≡ legend) together with `check:bundle`'s existing byte-identical
+  freshness guarantee, rather than a runtime version constant — no change to the
+  generated engine bundle, and the contract is checked in CI rather than asserted
+  at startup.
+
+*Rejected at the same review:* making the LSP emit *full* semantic tokens (instead
+of sparse corrections over the TextMate floor). It contradicts Decision 2 of this
+ADR — the floor must stand alone in no-LSP contexts (GitHub, `bat`, diffs) and full
+emission flattens the braces-vs-name distinction. The sparse split is kept; only
+its seam is gated (blocker 3).
+
+*Unchanged / still deferred:* the TextMate floor remains the guaranteed baseline
+(Community / no-LSP users are first-class); hover/completion stay post-1.0 on the
+ADR-023 substrate; JetBrains `defaultDialect` parity with VS Code and incremental
+`semanticTokens/range` are tracked but non-blocking. (Process note: the review's
+draft flagged a committed `editors/vscode/dist/` as a high risk; `git ls-files`
+shows it untracked — `.gitignore` covers `dist/` — so that finding was withdrawn.)

+// SPDX-License-Identifier: Apache-2.0
+//
+// Shared, pinned packaging helpers for the editor integrations (ADR-017, blocker
+// 3). The VS Code extension and the JetBrains plugin each assemble the SAME
+// self-contained `flatbars-lsp` server with esbuild; this module is the one place
+// that bundle step and the editor language set live, so the two packagers cannot
+// drift and cannot float onto an unpinned esbuild.
+import { resolve } from "node:path";
+
+// Pinned esbuild version — the same one `gen:bundle` pins for the engine bundle
+// (package.json: `npx esbuild@0.23.0`). One esbuild across the repo keeps the
+// shipped server bytes reproducible. Bump here AND in the gen:bundle script
+// together.
+export const ESBUILD_VERSION = "0.23.0";
+
+export function assertEsbuildVersion(esbuild) {
+  if (esbuild.version !== ESBUILD_VERSION) {
+    throw new Error(
+      `esbuild ${esbuild.version} is installed but the editor packagers pin ${ESBUILD_VERSION} ` +
+        `(see editors/shared/sync.mjs). Install the pinned version (npm i -D -E esbuild@${ESBUILD_VERSION}) ` +
+        `or, if the bump is intended, update ESBUILD_VERSION here and the gen:bundle script together.`,
+    );
+  }
+}
+
+// Bundle the engine-backed LSP server to one self-contained CJS file. CJS output:
+// the server embeds vscode-languageserver, which is CJS and dynamically `require`s
+// node builtins — that breaks under an ESM bundle. `repoRoot` is the monorepo root
+// (the directory holding `editors/`).
+export async function bundleServer(esbuild, { repoRoot, outfile, sourcemap = false }) {
+  assertEsbuildVersion(esbuild);
+  await esbuild.build({
+    entryPoints: [resolve(repoRoot, "editors", "lsp", "bin", "flatbars-lsp.mjs")],
+    bundle: true,
+    platform: "node",
+    format: "cjs",
+    sourcemap,
+    outfile,
+    logLevel: "warning",
+  });
+}
+
+// The editor language set — the `flatbars` umbrella plus one language per dialect,
+// native extensions only (not .hbs/.handlebars/.mustache). Single source for the
+// VS Code manifest (asserted by its smoke test) and the JetBrains TextMate bundle
+// manifest. All five share the one `source.flatbars` grammar.
+export const LANGUAGES = [
+  { id: "flatbars", aliases: ["FlatBars"], extensions: [".flatbars"] },
+  { id: "rawbars", aliases: ["RawBars"], extensions: [".rawbars"] },
+  { id: "minbars", aliases: ["MinBars"], extensions: [".minbars"] },
+  { id: "fullbars", aliases: ["FullBars"], extensions: [".fullbars"] },
+  { id: "maxbars", aliases: ["MaxBars"], extensions: [".maxbars"] },
+];
+
+export const LANGUAGE_IDS = LANGUAGES.map((l) => l.id);
